01  Mass timber

Accretech SBS

LocationPortland, Oregon
FirmOpen Concept Architecture
RoleSchematic design through construction administration
StructureGlulam frame, GLT floor and stair
Size30,000 sf · 2021–24

A mass timber manufacturing facility. I detailed the stair and worked on the exterior cladding studies in 3D.

Every connection here is a shop item landing on a wood member. The drawings had to be right before anything was cut, so the stair was worked out with the fabricator ahead of the shop drawings rather than corrected against them afterward.

This is the part of the work I want more of: the point where a drawing becomes a manufacturing instruction.

02  Fabricated assembly into existing work

PDX Enplaning East — Curtainwall & Revolving Door

LocationPortland, Oregon
FirmMWA Architects
ClientPort of Portland
RoleCurtainwall and entrance details, construction administration
StatusIn construction, 2024–26

Terminal East rehabilitation for the Port of Portland. A main airport entrance rebuilt into an existing opening with minimal dimensional tolerance, with the terminal in operation throughout. I drew the curtainwall and entrance details and worked them out in the field with the general contractor, the installers, and the door manufacturer.

A shop-built assembly going into a building that does not match its record drawings. The tolerance had to be resolved on paper before it could be resolved on site.

03  Repeated assemblies

Rooted at 19th

LocationRedmond, Oregon
FirmOpen Concept Architecture
RoleDesign modeling and BIM strategy
Size10 buildings · 22 dwelling units
Years2023–24

An affordable cottage cluster built from four unit plans. I led the design modeling and BIM strategy across the linked models and consultant files, and carried the sheets shown here in the Type 01 permit set.

E1 is a staggered-stud exterior wall at R-28, developed with the builder to cut framing time across ten buildings. The wall-to-floor detail resolves it against a glulam rimboard and an LSL sill, drawn to structural.

The reason to show a cottage cluster to a fabricator: the value is not in the building, it is in deciding once and repeating. Four plans, five configurations, one detail set, developed with the people who had to build it.

05  Assembly space

Oregon Tech CEET — Commons and Auditorium

LocationKlamath Falls, Oregon
FirmTVA Architects
RoleProduction lead, construction documents
Size70,000 sf · $30M
Completed2021

A classroom, laboratory, and administration building. I was production lead for the construction documents and detailed the central atrium, the commons and auditorium, and the applied technology labs.

The ceiling does the acoustic work: acoustical panels, black acoustical panels, and perforated metal, laid out against the AV speaker locations. I drew the reflected ceiling plans and worked the layout out with the acoustic and technology consultants.

Making the room work meant coordinating the ceiling, the mechanical distribution, and the AV layout in the same volume.

09  Venue

HAPO Community Stage

LocationRichland, Washington
FirmDesign West Architects
RoleDesign lead
ClientCity of Richland
Size6,000 sf · 2014–16

A permanent outdoor performance venue for the City of Richland. A 25-foot-high covered stage, an orchestra pit, a performer dressing room with a private restroom, and an enclosed electrical and storage room. Sound and lighting are built in, with truss connections left for touring equipment. The audience area is an excavated bowl that carries the acoustics.

My first venue, and the first time I worked with an AV consultant. The sound and lighting had to be built into the structure rather than added to it.
